absent: Full byte sizes offsets and alignment of control polynomial and formatting structures beyond observed field names.
Locking and concurrency rules for shared control handles and scratch polynomial reuse across threads.
Behavior of unrouted helpers for remainder copy multiply divide square log power root solving syndrome and locator computation and ECC encode and load.
Numeric values of BCH_MAX_M and BCH_MAX_T and fixed configuration parameters and error code integers and table base types.
Exact primitive polynomial default values and xi table semantics and generator polynomial bit layout beyond left justified grouping.
List versus plain bitmap output details and pointer rendering and width precision edge cases and bounded copy helper contract.
Allocation flag semantics and user copy guarantees and diagnostic output routing and warning macro effects.
Reentrancy and lifetime rules for formatted allocator temporaries and bitmap temporary buffers.

findings.text: Three symbols provide BCH codec lifecycle with external linkage. One creates a control handle from field order and correction power plus optional primitive polynomial and bit order flag. One decodes received data using supplied or internally derived syndromes and reports error count or failure. One releases a handle safely when given an absent handle or a live handle.

Two symbols expose bitmap text parsing with external linkage. One copies a user supplied buffer with termination guarantee then delegates to the core parser and releases the copy. The core parser converts a human readable hexadecimal representation with separators into machine words sized by requested bit count.

Two small utilities have external linkage. One maps a character holding hexadecimal meaning to its numeric value with a failure sentinel for other inputs. The other scans a bounded character sequence for a target value or terminator and returns the stopping position.

Three formatting symbols have external linkage. A variadic allocator forwards to a va list variant. The va list variant sizes output by an initial measurement pass then allocates and renders. The core renderer converts a format description plus arguments into a bounded character buffer and reports the would be length.

Four numeric rendering helpers have external linkage without static restriction in the fragments. One formats an integer according to field width precision base and flags. The others decompose decimal values into eight digit groups with exact or trimmed leading group handling using a digit pair table.

Control creation acts as an entry point that validates field order and correction power against supported ranges and a product bound, selects a default primitive polynomial when zero is supplied, allocates tables and scratch polynomials, builds field and encoding structures, and returns an absent handle after cleanup on any failure.

Decoding acts as an entry point that rejects oversize payloads, derives syndromes when not supplied with early success when received and calculated redundancy match, builds an error locator, searches roots, validates and remaps locations into data plus redundancy coordinates with optional within byte reflection, and reports count or a message integrity failure.

User bitmap parsing acts as an entry point that safely imports a user buffer of given length, treats import failure as its own error, parses with effectively unbounded input length, and always releases the temporary copy before returning.

Bounded formatting acts as an entry point that guards against oversize destination sizes, guarantees termination when size is positive, never writes past the supplied end, and returns the full would be length clamped into positive integer range.

Polynomial division requires dividend degree at least divisor degree to produce a nontrivial quotient. In that case the dividend is replaced by its remainder modulo the divisor and the quotient coefficients are taken from the upper portion of the transformed dividend. Otherwise the quotient is defined as zero polynomial.

Greatest common divisor orders operands by degree then repeatedly replaces the higher degree operand by its remainder modulo the lower and exchanges them until the lower becomes constant. The surviving operand is returned and debug tracing brackets the operation. The procedure mutates its inputs.

Trace remainder computation iterates exactly as many times as the field order. It maintains a scratch power of the indeterminate modulo the target polynomial and accumulates it into an output polynomial while squaring coefficients and reducing when needed. Log form of the modulus is prepared once and leading zero coefficients are trimmed at the end.

Factor attempt initializes the first output to the input polynomial and the second to absent, derives a trace polynomial for the supplied index, and only when that trace is nonconstant computes a gcd against a copy of the input. A proper divisor triggers division of the input and in place storage of both factors overlapping the original storage.

Root search dispatches degrees one through four to dedicated low degree solvers. Higher degrees use recursive splitting driven by an increasing trace index bounded by field order, accumulating counts from both factors with an offset for the second factor output area. Zero degree or out of range index yields no roots in the generic path.

Exhaustive search evaluates the candidate polynomial over a trailing window of field powers whose size combines payload bit length and redundancy bit count. It uses logarithmic coefficient form with a normalized constant term, records complemented positions of vanishing evaluations, stops early once as many roots as degree are found, and reports zero unless the full degree count is reached.

Field table construction rejects a primitive polynomial whose degree does not match the configured field order and rejects nonprimitive candidates where the multiplicative order closes early. On success it fills power and logarithm tables for all nonzero field sizes, defines power at full period as one, and defines log of zero as zero.

Byte division table construction clears a table sized by four byte positions times all byte values times redundancy words, then for each value and position computes the remainder of the shifted monomial multiple modulo the generator using repeated highest set bit elimination and wordwise folding.

Quadratic solver base construction first locates an exponent whose trace is nonzero, then searches field elements for solutions to the canonical quadratic equation adjusted by that trace element, records one solution per basis index, and reports failure if any index remains without a solution.

Generator construction marks cyclotomic cosets of odd exponents up to twice the correction power, builds the product of corresponding first degree terms by field multiplication, derives redundancy bit count from resulting degree, and stores a left justified binary image grouped into machine words. Allocation failure yields an absent result after releasing temporaries.

Initialization enforces field order within a small supported interval starting at five, correction power within a positive bound and product bound relative to field size, and optional fixed parameter configuration with diagnostic output on mismatch. Any allocation or table build failure funnels through a single release path returning an absent handle.

Core bitmap parsing scans from the end of the supplied range up to a newline, repeatedly trims separators then consumes up to eight hexadecimal digits into successive machine words from low to high, respects big endian pairing on wide builds, fails when input needs more words than available, clears unused trailing bits, and fails if significant bits appear beyond the requested length.

Reverse word extraction accumulates at most eight hexadecimal digits from the end backwards, stops at the start boundary or a separator, reports invalid character on nonhex input, and reports overflow when a ninth hexadecimal digit would belong to the same word.

Region boundary test treats whitespace and comma as separators. Reverse region location repeatedly steps the end pointer backwards while it points at such separators, yielding the last significant character of the preceding region.

Bounded character search advances while remaining length permits and neither terminator nor target has been met, then returns the stopping pointer which may point at the target, at the terminator, or at the bound end.

Hexadecimal decoding uses branchless arithmetic over the input character and its uppercased form to map decimal digits and letter digits in either case to their numeric values, yielding a negative sentinel for all other inputs.

Bitmap rendering selects list or plain representation based on a flag, formats through the kernel formatted allocator with bit count and mask arguments plus newline, copies through a helper honoring file offset and caller length including termination handling, releases the temporary, and propagates allocation failure distinctly from copy size.

List based formatted allocation measures required length with a copied argument list, allocates one extra byte for termination through a tracked caller allocator, renders a second time into the allocation, warns when the two measurements disagree, and returns an absent result on allocation failure.

Bounded formatting rejects oversize sizes with a one time warning and zero result, normalizes the end pointer to never precede the start, copies literal spans with truncation awareness, decodes numeric width precision character string pointer and percent directives through dedicated helpers, advances past alphanumeric pointer suffixes, terminates when size permits, and returns full length excluding terminator clamped to positive range.

Integer rendering derives sign and prefix needs from flags, adjusts field width for sign and alternate form, generates digits in reverse using direct table lookup for small values and shifting for power of two bases or decimal grouping otherwise, then emits leading spaces, sign, prefix, padding, precision zeros, digits, and trailing spaces while never writing past the supplied end.

Decimal decomposition splits wide values into eight digit blocks using division for high blocks and a trimmed final block. Full block rendering always emits eight digits including leading zeros while trimmed rendering omits leading zeros, both using precomputed digit pairs and fixed point reciprocal division.

Control structure observed through usage carries m for field order, t for correction power, n for code length, ecc_bits and ecc_bytes for redundancy sizes, swap_bits flag, a_pow_tab and a_log_tab tables, mod8_tab table, ecc_buf and ecc_buf2 buffers, xi_tab table, syn and cache arrays, elp storage, and poly_2t scratch array.

Polynomial structure observed through usage carries deg for degree plus c for coefficients. A gf_poly_deg1 overlay enables in place factor storage. Scratch instances are sized for twice the correction power and zeroed to the modulus degree when needed.

Formatting structures observed through usage include printf_spec carrying flags and base plus field_width and precision, and fmt carrying str and state. Decoded state distinguishes FORMAT_STATE_NONE plus FORMAT_STATE_NUM plus FORMAT_STATE_WIDTH plus FORMAT_STATE_PRECISION plus FORMAT_STATE_CHAR plus FORMAT_STATE_STR plus FORMAT_STATE_PTR plus FORMAT_STATE_PERCENT_CHAR with fallback abort.

Formatting proceeds as a loop of decode then dispatch. Literal state copies a span. Numeric state consumes an integer argument of appropriate width. Width and precision states consume integer arguments to adjust the specification. Character string pointer and percent states emit their respective forms. Unknown state aborts to termination handling.

Root location behaves as degree dispatch with recursive splitting. Low degrees terminate in specialized solvers. Higher degrees attempt factoring then recurse on each factor with incremented trace index, combining counts. Termination occurs on low degree, zero degree, or trace index exceeding field order.

Decoding proceeds through validation, syndrome acquisition, locator construction, root search, and location remapping. Early exit reports success when redundancy matches. Locator failure skips search. Root count mismatch or out of range location converts to integrity failure. Otherwise the locator degree is reported as error count.

Several polynomial helpers mutate inputs. Remainder computation overwrites the dividend. Greatest common divisor mutates both operands via repeated remainders. Trace computation mutates scratch and output polynomials. Factoring clobbers the input polynomial to store both outputs in place and uses shared scratch slots that are not reentrant.

An alternate root search definition is a macro that ignores its k argument and captures len from the caller scope to invoke exhaustive search. Use outside a scope defining that name fails or binds the wrong value, and switching between function and macro changes behavior from trace factoring to exhaustive evaluation.

Allocation helper signals failure through err flag set on absent return rather than through the return value alone. Callers must initialize the flag, check it after a batch of allocations, and funnel failures to cleanup. Generator construction additionally releases partial temporaries before returning an absent result.

Decoded locations are initially in reversed codeword coordinates and must be reflected around total bit length then optionally reflected within each byte depending on stored bit order. Any location at or beyond total length invalidates the whole result. Callers must provide output space for up to the locator degree entries.

Bitmap parsing distinguishes invalid characters from excess input. Nonhex digits yield invalid argument, while more words than fit or significant bits beyond requested length yield overflow. Callers must size the destination for the full requested bit count and must not assume partial results on error.

Formatting never overruns the destination but return value reports full length even when truncated, so callers must compare return against size to detect loss. Oversize requests are rejected with zero rather than truncated. Callers relying on two pass sizing must handle a warning path where repeated measurement disagrees.

Minimum field order is five with upper bound BCH_MAX_M and correction power bounded above by BCH_MAX_T plus a product bound against code length. Code length derives from field order as power of two minus one. Redundancy storage derives from field order times correction power rounded to word and byte granularity. Byte division table spans four byte positions over all byte values.

Decoding reports EINVAL for oversize payloads or missing buffers and EBADMSG when locator and root handling fails. Bitmap parsing reports EINVAL for bad digits and EOVERFLOW for excess words or excess significant bits. Bitmap rendering reports ENOMEM on allocation failure. Formatting clamps to INT_MAX and user parsing passes UINT_MAX as input bound.

Numeric formatting supports bases eight ten and sixteen with SPECIAL prefix handling and SMALL controlling case. SIGN PLUS SPACE select sign output while LEFT and ZEROPAD select padding. Decimal grouping operates on eight digit blocks with thresholds at one hundred and powers of ten up to one hundred million.
